Delegate `jookoi-paper-trail`'s mechanical half to a fork subagent

Delegate `jookoi-paper-trail`'s mechanical half to a **fork** subagent, so a flush stops eating main context — the judgement half (what happened, why, does it duplicate or invalidate an existing entry) is untransferable and stays in the main thread; the mechanics (read `SKILL.md`, read `TODO.md`/`BACKLOG.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`, find the anchor, apply, keep the format) are 3+ large files that are permanent in context once read and never looked at again — already the delegation trigger named in global `AGENTS.md`. Must be a fork, not a general-purpose agent: a cold agent has no access to what happened this session, which is the skill's entire input, and would need that summary written into its prompt anyway; a fork inherits the context and keeps its tool output out of the parent. Contract the fork needs: the facts as bullets with the why, an explicit file/section allowlist, a standing fence around `TODO.md`'s `## Context` and any "do not re-derive" block (the most expensive institutional memory and the easiest thing for an agent to tidy away), "report, don't write" when unsure an item already exists, and a receipt naming each file plus the exact anchor text matched — verified by targeted `grep` from the parent, never by trusting the receipt. Boundaries: chunk-boundary only, never concurrent with parent edits to the same files (lost writes), and not worth the overhead for a single checklist tick. Open: whether it ships as a `/flush` slash command that packages brief + fences + receipt contract, and whether `flush` and plain append want different fences. Adjacent to the "which judgement steps become mechanical" question in the item above, but a different mechanism — this delegates the work, it does not mechanize it

Graphify output — vault-mirror pattern for no-commit repos

Corrected 2026-08-30: graphify output is not cheap to regenerate (LLM-backed extraction — this repo's own `gr` script now targets the `claude` backend, reconfigured 2026-09-01 off Ollama; `gr:ollama` and `gr:gemini` kept as alternates) and carries a hand-curated layer on top (`graphify save-result`/`reflect` → `LESSONS.md`, `.graphify_learning.json` preference overlay) — not disposable output, closer to an authored artifact.
- **Own repos, commit allowed** — tracked normally in `_architecture/graphify/`, no prefix, no vault involvement.

- **Restricted/no-commit repos** — private, at `_jookoi-architecture/graphify/` in the checkout, mirrored into the existing vault location `repo-mirrors/<repo-name>/graphify/` — same per-repo keying as everything else, no new taxonomy.

- **Sync semantics differ deliberately from `vault-sync.js`.** That script's mtime-diff/conflict-report machinery exists because markdown notes have real partial-merge value. A generated graph doesn't — it's one artifact from one run, so blunt whole-folder overwrite is correct, not a shortcut. Needs its own small script (or a distinct `--blunt` path), not a mode bolted onto `vault-sync.js`.

- **One-directional, matching the single-canonical-instance work-PC pattern:** one designated checkout runs the expensive extraction; that checkout's output is authoritative and overwrites the vault copy. Other parallel checkouts read from the vault, never write to it.

- **Still open before building anything:** confirm `graph.json`/`LESSONS.md` don't embed machine-specific absolute paths (test via the cheap `--code-only` extraction, not a full LLM run) — if they do, the mirrored copy isn't portable across machines and the pattern needs a path-rewrite step.

Personal-dev-stack setup as two skills, not a rigid script

Reconsidered (supersedes the earlier single-skill framing — merged here to avoid duplication). Setup/sync across machines and repos should be skill-guided (orchestration + judgement, interactive — the skill asks the user whenever it's uncertain about a preference or the machine's state, never guesses silently), not one rigid install script or copy-paste procedure. Targeted mechanical scripts stay in scope underneath it (e.g. package.json's skill-folder symlink step for harnesses that don't read global .agents/skills) but the skill owns reading the environment and editing things like a repo-local AGENTS.md for that repo's stack. Key requirement carried over: when a setup step touches a shared file the user already owns (e.g. `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`), never overwrite wholesale — read what's there, propose a merge/diff, let the user accept or reject.
Splits into two skills by level, not one umbrella:

- **Computer-level (global/vault) setup skill.** Governs a machine's copy of the personal vault repo. At home there's already one running instance using the private non-commit (`_jookoi-`) path; work computers need this skill to bootstrap the same thing following that suffix/version convention. Scope: push-to-vault and pull-from-vault scripts, deduplication when multiple checkouts of the same repo name exist in different locations or on different branches, setting up or updating the AGENTS.md files, copying global skills and other global-setup content out from this repo's `my-global-setup/` into the machine's real global folders.

- **Repo-level setup skill.** Governs one target repo's own scaffolding — paper-trail folders, per-repo AGENTS.md flavouring, whatever else a repo needs once the machine-level baseline already exists. Narrower and mostly already scoped by the existing TODO item on folding `_jookoi-architecture/` scaffolding into `jookoi-paper-trail.js` as a subcommand — that item is (or becomes) part of this skill, not a separate thing.

Update-to-latest-version mode (fingerprinting a machine's last-synced state against this repo) is explicitly deferred — stretch goal, manual updates for now until there's a clearer read on what's actually needed.
Still open: what else the computer-level skill needs to do beyond the items listed above — scope isn't closed yet.

Before designing: research pass via cowork on how other personal/AI-tooling setup systems handle this reliably (idempotent setup, dotfiles-style bootstrapping, interactive/ask-on-uncertainty flows) rather than reinventing it blind.
